newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jiangling wins status of foreign-invested firm.
newsitem.headline: Jiangling wins status of foreign-invested firm.

text.p: Jiangling Motors Corporation Ltd said on Thursday it had been classified as a foreign-funded company due to its issue of B shares.
In a statement in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times, Jiangling said the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Co-operation had approved it to become a foreign-invested enterprise.
Trading in Jiangling's A and B shares was suspended on Thursday morning after the announcement and will resume in the afternoon.
Jiangling issued 174 million B shares last year.

At that time, Jiangling said it had a total of 693.21 million outstanding shares, comprising 353.24 million state shares, 174.0 million B shares, 117.6 million A shares and 48.37 million legal person shares.
Ford Motor Co owns 20 percent of Jiangling.

A company spokesman told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin Jiangling obtained the new status because its B shares accounted for more than 25 percent of its total share capital. B shares now represent 25.10 percent of Jiangling's outstanding shares, the firm said in the statement.
The status will entitle Jiangling to preferential treatment, such as greater flexibility in raising funds, the spokesman said but did not elaborate.
Usually, a foreign-invested firm is assessed at a 7.5 percent tax rate for several years, while most listed firms, including Jiangling, are assessed at 15 percent.
